predecessors.name: Kingdom of Allada
predecessors.text: the Abomey Plateau, settled by Aja from Allada c.

successors.name: French Africa
successors.text: the kingdom, made 'a French protectorate in 1894'; the kingdom under Agoli-agbo lasted as a protectorate to 1904 when it became French Dahomey

ledger.x: c. 1600: the Kingdom of Dahomey is founded on the Abomey Plateau. 'The Kingdom of Dahomey was established around 1600 as an offshoot of the royal dynasty of the Kingdom of Allada'; infobox 'Aja settlers from Allada settle on Abomey Plateau: c. 1600'. The page treats Houegbadja (c. 1645-1685) as the foundational king.
c. 1620: Dakodonou begins the conquest of the Abomey Plateau. Infobox: 'Dakodonu begins conquest on Abomey Plateau: c. 1620'. The 10,000 km2 infobox area of 1700 is the plateau at its first extent.
1724 (30 March): Agaja takes Allada, the mother kingdom.
1726 (14 April): Oyo sends its army against Dahomey and sacks Abomey.
1727 (26 February): Agaja takes Whydah, the slave-trading port.
1730 (about): the Whydah exiles try to retake the coast.
1730: Dahomey becomes a tributary of Oyo.
1734: the last Whydah faction is beaten.
1740: the Oyo war ends with Agaja's death.
1823: Dahomey stops paying tribute to Oyo.
1861: Porto-Novo is named as one of Dahomey's tributaries.
1890 (4 March): Dahomey storms the French stockade at Cotonou.
1890 (3 October): Dahomey cedes Cotonou to France.
1890 (3 October): the first war ends in a treaty.
1894: Dahomey is reduced and made a French protectorate.
1894 (January): the independent Kingdom of Dahomey ends; a French protectorate with Agoli-agbo as king runs to 1904.

wars.name: Dahomean conquest of Allada
wars.outcome: Dahomey won: Agaja's army entered Allada on 30 March 1724 and took Godomey in April.

wars.name: Dahomean conquest of Whydah
wars.outcome: Dahomey won: Whydah attacked 26 February 1727, palace burned; the exiles under Huffon failed to retake it (Huffon d.

wars.name: Oyo invasions of Dahomey
wars.outcome: Oyo sacked Abomey in 1726 and invaded again in 1728, 1729 and 1730; Dahomey became a tributary state with the boundary at the Ouémé River, and Agaja sent his son Tegbessou to Oyo as a guarantee; war resumed in 1739 and ended 1740.

wars.name: Dahomean war against the Mahi
wars.outcome: A war against the Mahi people, north of Abomey, began in 1731; the Agaja page gives no outcome or land.

wars.name: First Franco-Dahomean War
wars.outcome: French victory: Cotonou ceded and Porto-Novo recognised as a French protectorate in the treaty of 3 October 1890.

wars.name: Second Franco-Dahomean War
wars.outcome: French victory: Abomey entered 17 November 1892; Béhanzin surrendered 15 January 1894 and was exiled to Martinique; Dahomey became a French protectorate.

certainty.note: No frontier line is given by the pages; the Ouémé River boundary with Oyo after 1730 (Agaja page) and the Cotonou cession of 3 October 1890 are the only treaty-fixed edges, and neither is drawn sharp.
